name: John F. Kennedy
description: US president associated with the New Frontier, civil-rights proposals and Cold War diplomacy.
scope: Public positions and conduct during the specified period; this represents the individual rather than all party members or citizens.

axes.brief: Electoral and constitutional institutions structured his presidency.
axes.counter: Initial caution on voting rights limits an idealised universal-democracy reading.

axes.brief: Civil-rights protection coexisted with surveillance and anti-communist security policy.
axes.counter: Federal protection of demonstrators did not imply support for all disruptive gatherings.

axes.brief: He argued for immigrants’ contributions and equal civil membership.
axes.counter: Period integration language differs from contemporary multicultural service policy.

axes.brief: He advocated immigration reform away from discriminatory national-origin quotas.
axes.counter: The modern unlimited settlement and welfare claims remain extrapolations.

axes.brief: Cuba intervention and Vietnam advisers coexisted with missile-crisis compromise and test-ban diplomacy.
axes.counter: He avoided invasion during the missile crisis rather than rejecting military power.

axes.brief: Alliances and international aid mattered while US sovereign authority remained.
axes.counter: Multilateral activity does not entail binding international criminal jurisdiction.

axes.brief: Private enterprise coexisted with public investment and proposed publicly financed healthcare.
axes.counter: Medicare proposals were not a demand that every healthcare provider be public.

axes.brief: Trade liberalisation and negotiation accompanied domestic competitiveness.
axes.counter: National-security and adjustment concerns qualified complete unilateral removal.

axes.brief: Private markets, growth-oriented tax cuts and federal development programmes coexisted.
axes.counter: Steel-price intervention and wage policy complicate a pure market reading.

axes.brief: Poverty and regional development proposals coexisted with tax cuts to stimulate growth.
axes.counter: The Great Society’s later expansion is not attributed to Kennedy.

axes.brief: He expressly defended political independence from the Catholic hierarchy.
axes.counter: Religious public language and customary ceremonies remained.

axes.brief: Civil-rights change coexisted with conventional marriage and sexual norms of his period.
axes.counter: General reformism cannot establish modern marriage or abortion positions.

axes.brief: Space exploration and development were priorities alongside nuclear fallout concerns.
axes.counter: No direct AI or enhancement policy exists for this period.

axes.brief: Federal enforcement of civil rights challenged resistant state governments.
axes.counter: Constitutional state and local powers remained outside those conflicts.

reasons.4: The scoped national institutions retained constitutional states with their own governmental constitutions. Federal programme supremacy does not remove that protected institutional role.
reasons.5: State and local police retained ordinary jurisdiction. National security coordination does not establish support for replacing them with a single national police authority.

axes.brief: His social-opportunity explanations foregrounded education and discrimination.
axes.counter: Those explanations do not establish a complete behavioural-genetics theory.
axes.gap: Modern causal questions are low-confidence analogies; support for civil rights alone does not settle biological differences.
